name: IST 407 — Machine Learning

vscode._comment_python_envs: python.useEnvironmentsExtension=false is LOAD-BEARING, not tuning. ms-python.python lists ms-python.vscode-python-envs in its extensionPack, so requesting the Python extension silently installs the Environments extension for every student. Measured 2026-08-20 in the student container: the Python extension activated it by API ('activationEvent: api, root cause: ms-python.python') and it then resolved the SAME interpreter /usr/local/bin/python 242 times in 117 seconds -- 45 of them in the 2 seconds after a second notebook was opened -- saturating the resolve queue until getActivePythonEnvironment blew its 2000ms budget and the window appeared to hang. Its package.json default is already false, so something (an experiment rollout) turns it on; setting it explicitly pins it off. Requires a window reload to take effect. Extension hosts in the same container with it inactive: zero timeouts, two notebooks clean.
vscode._comment_pylance: languageServerMode=light: Pylance was isolated 2026-08-20 as the cause of the second-notebook stall (disable Pylance -> stall gone; re-enable -> stall returns; downgrading one version did not help). Signature: the remote extension host went unresponsive in 40s-of-every-60s episodes, all recovering on a 60s tick phase-locked to extension-host start, while the container sat idle (load 0.19, no blocked I/O) and both notebook kernels started fine -- i.e. the host was blocked on its language server, not computing. 'light' drops workspace-wide indexing and cross-file symbol search, which buy little in a 126-file teaching repo, and keeps the completions and hover on pandas/numpy/sklearn that students actually use. NOTE python.analysis.indexing was still true in the deployed template during every repro, so indexing had never actually been off. If light is insufficient, next steps in order: python.analysis.nodeExecutable (Pylance otherwise runs its server on the Node bundled with VS Code, the known dev-container failure mode), then python.languageServer=Jedi, then disable Pylance.
